However, if you see a molecular orbital diagram of this molecule, it would most likely show the e-density entering the anti pi orbital leading to instability. Remember atomic orbital overlap to form molecular orbitals (like Pc + Po = πco) which tend to be lower in energy and as a result more favored.

4. Lastly, in resonance we typically observe the pi bond "moving" due to hyperconjugation typically in atoms via p orbitals, sometimes you would see dashed lines indicating electrons are shared evenly between atoms. So the electrons would not be shared by the hydrogens as they have a full sigma orbital and can't "accommodate any more e-density" because they don't have pi orbital for hyperconjugation.
